title: Grateful Dead Live at Boston Music Hall on 1971-04-07

ai_review.summary: Stunning Betty Cantor soundboard capture of a rare, high‑energy April 1971 show with a smoking St. Stephen and China>Rider sequence.
ai_review.review: The recording is crystal‑clear, with the iconic plug‑in of Garcia’s guitar and a sweet, balanced mix that showcases the band at peak form. The performance is a “rocker from start to finish,” highlighted by a rare St. Stephen, a blazing China Cat Sunflower > I Know You Rider, and an explosive post‑drum jam, though the tape unfortunately cuts off just as the second‑set momentum peaks.

ai_rating.rationale: Overwhelmingly positive reviews praise both the musical fire and the superb soundboard quality; only a few note an incomplete ending, keeping the rating just shy of perfect.

recording_quality.technical_notes: Crisp, sweet mix with clear guitar plug‑in and pedal sounds; praised as “stunning quality.” Minor complaint about the tape ending abruptly, but no significant audio flaws.

standout_songs: China Cat Sunflower > I Know You Rider
show_quality.setlist_flow: First set opens with a driving rock feel; second set rolls into a long boogie, kicking off with China>Rider into St. Stephen and moving through Hard to Handle before a thrilling drum segment that unfortunately fades out.

band_member_comments.Jerry: Garcia’s guitar plug‑in is noted; his break from Not Fade Away into an epic jam receives high praise.
band_member_comments.Phil: Bass on St. Stephen described as rumbling the plant off the mantle – a classic ‘Phil bomb.’
band_member_comments.Drums: The drum segment and ensuing jam are highlighted as a standout moment.
